questions.q: Which expression gives a random whole number between 1 and 6 inclusive?
questions.feedback: randint includes both ends, so 1 to 6 is exactly a dice roll.

questions.q: State what is meant by a pseudo-random number.

markPoints.concept: it is produced by an algorithm, so it is not truly random
markPoints.exemplar: It is produced by an algorithm, so it only appears random.

questions.example: A number produced by an algorithm that appears random but is not truly random, because the same starting value would produce the same sequence again.
questions.paraphrase: It comes out of a formula rather than from chance, so it merely looks random.
questions.feedback: Produced by a calculation, therefore only apparently random.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 6 — Chance machine, station 2: Generating a random number

questions.q: Explain why a program that shuffles a deck of cards for a gambling site should not use an ordinary pseudo-random number generator.

markPoints.concept: the sequence is produced by an algorithm and can be predicted
markPoints.exemplar: The sequence comes from an algorithm and can be predicted.

markPoints.concept: so someone who worked it out could cheat
markPoints.exemplar: So someone who worked it out could cheat.

questions.example: A pseudo-random sequence comes out of an algorithm, so anyone who learned the starting value could work out which cards were coming next, and could use that to cheat.
questions.paraphrase: Because the numbers are generated by a formula they can be predicted, which would let a player who had deduced it gain an unfair advantage.
questions.feedback: Predictable, and then what being predictable makes possible here.
